about: Twenty questions for the W9 SOP assistant. Each is scored on two axes: is the answer right (every must_contain string appears, case insensitive), and is the citation right (every expected_sources file is cited, and no superseded file is presented as current). expect_decline items pass only if the assistant says the SOPs do not cover it and cites nothing. Drafted by Claude 2026-09-26, reviewed against the SOPs by Mario the same day.

items.question: What is the minimum mezzanine bitrate for a feature?
items.expected_answer: 20 Mbps.

items.question: Which video codecs are accepted for a mezzanine file?
items.expected_answer: H.264 High Profile or Apple ProRes 422 HQ, and no other codec.

items.question: What bitrate is the 720p rung of the encoding ladder?
items.expected_answer: 3.5 Mbps.

items.question: An episode was supplied with a UHD source. Does it get a 2160p rung?
items.expected_answer: No. Only features supplied with a 3840x2160 mezzanine get the 2160p rung; episodes, trailers and promos never do, even from a UHD source.

items.question: What is the maximum number of characters per caption line?
items.expected_answer: 32 characters, and at most 2 lines per caption.

items.question: Does a 10 second promo need captions?
items.expected_answer: No. Promos need captions only when longer than 15 seconds.

items.question: What should the mezzanine filename be for version 1 of TT-0142, Harbor Lights season 2 episode 7?
items.expected_answer: TT-0142_HarborLights_S02E07_MEZZ_v01.mov

items.question: How far before go live does an episode have to be delivered?
items.expected_answer: 5 business days.

items.question: When is an asset considered at risk?
items.expected_answer: When its deadline is less than 48 hours away and its status is anything other than delivered.

items.question: A delivery deadline works out to land on a Saturday. What happens?
items.expected_answer: It moves back to the previous Friday. Deadlines never fall on a weekend.

items.question: How many times can an asset be redelivered before it needs special approval, and whose?
items.expected_answer: Twice. A third redelivery needs approval from the Post Production Supervisor.

items.question: How quickly must a redelivery reach the platform?
items.expected_answer: Within 72 hours of the fix being approved.

items.question: Three assets failed QC in the last hour. Who do I page?
items.expected_answer: Tier 1, the Media Operations on call. Three or more QC failures in an hour usually means an encoder or ingest fault.

items.question: What's the SLA for clearing a QC hold?
items.expected_answer: 24 hours, calendar hours including weekends. The 48 hour business hours SLA is from the superseded 2025 edition.

items.question: Can the operator who raised a QC hold clear it themselves?
items.expected_answer: No. Only the QC Lead on shift can clear a hold (version 3.0). The 2025 edition let the operator clear it, but that edition is superseded.
items.review_note: No guildline about operator QC hold clear

items.question: Can a caption failure be waived to hit a deadline?
items.expected_answer: No. Caption failures cannot be waived. (The superseded 2025 edition allowed it.)

items.question: A promo has been sitting in qc_hold for 5 hours. What should have happened by now?
items.expected_answer: It should already have been escalated: promo holds escalate after 4 hours rather than 24, and an uncleared hold goes to Tier 2.

items.question: An episode's mezzanine arrives at 6 Mbps. What happens to it?
items.expected_answer: It goes to qc_hold, because the episode minimum is 8 Mbps. The hold must then be cleared or escalated within 24 hours, and a spec failure cannot be waived.

items.question: What is the target loudness for programme audio?
items.expected_answer: Not covered by the SOPs. The assistant should say so and not give a number.

items.question: Which cloud provider runs our encoders?
items.expected_answer: Not covered by the SOPs. The assistant should say so and not guess.
